title: Border Ambassador: tenant-aware EU residency routing and allow/deny precedence
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a ‘Border Ambassador’ routing policy component that evaluates tenant-scoped residency constraints, EU-only delivery requirements, and tenant allowlists/denylists. The ambassador will sit in the smart-routing pipeline and produce a deterministic route decision (region + tier + model variant) with clear precedence rules, audit annotations, and an emergency passthrough mechanism for support/debugging.
rationale: Current routing heuristics are brittle when tenants specify conflicting residency and allow/deny rules. We need a single, well-documented evaluator that encodes precedence (contractual residency > tenant blocklists > region performance tiers) and emits auditable decisions for compliance reviews and incident postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: Border Ambassador evaluates tenant residency metadata (tenant residency claim + account-level override) and enforces EU-only routing when requested.
Allowlist entries for a tenant permit routing to non-EU variants; denylists should block specific model families or instance tiers and escalate to fallback behavior.
Decision output includes structured audit fields: chosen_region, chosen_tier, chosen_model_variant, matched_rule_id, fallback_reason, decision_timestamp.
Policy precedence documented: contractual residency > tenant-enforced residency flag > global operator lockdown > allowlist > denylist > performance-tier fallback.
Integration tests exercising conflicting rules (e.g., tenant allowlist vs EU-only flag) pass in CI and simulated canary traffic.
Telemetry events emitted for every decision with sample-rate configuration and a linked trace ID for request sampling.
Emergency passthrough gate exists and is logged; gate has RBAC controls and audit trail for enable/disable actions.
SLO impact analysis completed; no increase in 95p latency > 8ms for routing decision in the happy path.
technical_design: Component: Border Ambassador runs as a stateless policy evaluator invoked inside the request routing path before shard selection.

Inputs: tenant_id, tenant_metadata (residency_claims, allowlist/denylist entries), request_headers (origin country hint, explicit-residency header), system_flags (operator lockdown), route_context (load/latency hints).
Outputs: flat routing decision and ordered evidence list (rule ids). Evidence is emitted as a small array of rule identifiers attached to audit logs.

Precedence: 1) contract-residency bindings from customer config store; 2) tenant-residency flag; 3) operator-level emergency lockdown; 4) tenant allowlist; 5) tenant denylist; 6) tier routing heuristics (latency/cost); 7) model-variant fallback mapping.

Fallback algorithm: when requested region/tier is unavailable, Ambassador attempts allowed compatible variants in the same region, then same continent, then operator-specified emergency fallback (only if allowlist allows it). All steps annotated with fallback_reason codes.
Security: RBAC enforced for allowlist/denylist edits; audit log retention 1 year for residency decisions; KMS-protected config snapshots for contractual residency bindings.
Observability: emit 'ambassador.decision' metric with tags chosen_region, chosen_tier, tenant_id, decision_outcome; include a sampled event to trace service graphs.
Policy Storage: tenant policies stored in Config DB as versioned rows; Ambassador caches policies with TTL and subscribes to change notifications to avoid stale enforcement.
Testing: unit policy tests, integration harness with simulated replica pools, and chaos test that kills preferred pools to validate fallback correctness.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (API + evaluator): implement evaluation tree with feature flags to flip precedence logic for experiments.
Phase 2 (caching + scale): add local LRU cache in Ambassador instances and changefeed listener to invalidate entries on policy updates.
Phase 3 (RBAC + UI): expose allowlist/denylist edit flows in Console with audit UI and operator lockdown toggle.
Backwards compatibility: default behavior must match existing routing for tenants without residency metadata; Ambassador should be a no-op when no policy exists.
Edge cases: ambiguous residency claims (multi-region consent) must default to the most restrictive region selection and record justification.
test_plan: Unit tests for precedence logic covering 30+ rule combinations.
Integration tests in staging that spin up EU and non-EU pools and assert routing decisions for 2000 synthetic tenant requests per minute.
Canary rollout to 5% of routing traffic for tenants with 'opt-in-ambassador' tag, monitor decision latency and correctness.
Chaos: simulate regional pool outage during canary and verify correct fallback code paths and audit logs.
Compliance verification with PM: generate sample audit reports for 10 tenants with residency constraints and validate exported CSV schema.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged merge: default OFF for all live tenants.
Internal rollout: enable for dev tenants and test accounts; run 48-hour soak.
Canary: enable for 5% routing traffic for tenants that opted in; monitor metrics and errors for 72 hours.
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% for opt-in tenants, then offer console toggle for broader tenant opt-in.
Operator lockdown toggle to temporarily force EU-only routing for all traffic during regulatory incidents.
Post-rollout: run audit report and adjust policy precedence if observed mismatches are found.
